newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE WHEAT FALLS ON MORE GOOD RAIN IN SE AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: SFE WHEAT FALLS ON MORE GOOD RAIN IN SE AUSTRALIA.

text.p: The Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures fell convincingly on Friday after further good overnight rain.
The fall, by about A$4.00 a tonne, followed overnight rain across Australia's southern and eastern grainbelt.
This brought areas which had been hard-hit by months of drought because of the El Nino weather pattern at least two nights of good rain, brokers noted.
In South Australia, last night's fall postponed culling of the crop, Chris Gray of C, A & L Bell Commodities said.

South Australian, Victorian and southern New South Wales wheat areas received 10 millimetres to 20 millimetres of rain overnight. Rainfall was widespread across areas which had been hardest-hit by the drought, brokers noted.
In Friday SFE floor trading, November 1997 and January 1998 both fell by A$4.00 a tonne to A$198.00 and A$195.50 respectively. March 1998 traded down by A$2.50 to A$198.50.
Turnover was solid with a total of 34 contracts sold.
The options focus was on January 1998 calls, with two lots sold at a A$190.00 strike price, eight lots at a A$205.00 strike and three lots at a A$210.00 strike price.
